title: ‘Hated’ Drug Company Head Arrested by FBI

image.attribution: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
A U.S. businessman once described as the “most hated man in America” was arrested.

Martin Shkreli was arrested at his New York City apartment, said federal prosecutor Robert Capers.

Shkreli, 32, heads New York-based Turing Pharmaceuticals.

He and his company were criticized after raising the price of a drug used by patients with AIDS and forms of cancer. The price of the drug “Daraprim” increased from $13.50 a pill to $700 a pill. The drug is used all over the world, including Africa.

The BBC described him as the “the worst man in America.”

After the criticism, Shkreli agreed to reduce the price of the cancer/AIDS drug. But recent reports by Forbes and other news organizations said Shkreli has since changed his mind about lowering the price.

Shkreli headed the drug firm Retrophin until 2014. Capers said that Shkreli used that company to pay off “his own personal debts.”
